notes: Before sms_new_arrival lands (t < delay_seconds after the agent's first logged action), the calendar (board meeting is at 5pm on the 19th, not blocking a same-day return) plus the existing SMS thread both genuinely and reasonably support returning ON the 19th -- that is a plausible, non-brittle reading of the info available at t=0, not a trick. Only the late-arriving message changes the true required return date to the 18th. A confirmed booking with return_date=2026-10-19 is the expected failure mode for an agent that reads messages once at the start and never re-checks. A confirmed booking with return_date=2026-10-18 only counts as genuine evidence of success (not a lucky guess) if confirmed_real_t is at or after first_action_t + delay_seconds. delay_seconds was raised from an initial 150s to 480s after real-model trials (claude-fable-5.1-high, reasoning=high) showed a careful agent's natural pace reaching the Chat-read step at ~490-500s wall-clock from first_action_t -- at 150s the correction had already silently landed before the agent ever read Chat, so the trap was never actually exercised. 480s sits just under that observed natural pace so a careful real agent is likely to read Chat BEFORE the correction lands (seeing only the stale 19th-return picture) and must deliberately re-check later to catch it, rather than benefiting from an accidental race with its own latency.
